title: Streaming batch interrupt arbitration with soft-state tenant shares and adaptive KV trimming
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Continuous batching improves throughput but interacts badly with long-lived KV working sets and tenants that have bursty latency-sensitive traffic. Current hard-preempt policies either penalize latency-sensitive tenants (high tail latency when preempted) or preserve KV state at cost of resource starvation for others.

Proposal: Implement an interrupt arbitration protocol for streaming/continuous batches that: (1) maintains soft-state tenant shares (a decaying credit balance) to guide preemption decisions, (2) proactively trims KV cache residency for low-value cold entries under memory pressure using adaptive heuristics, and (3) applies interrupt cooldowns and progressive degradation to avoid thrash. The design is SLO-aware — the scheduler uses tenant-configured latency envelopes (P50/P95 targets) and realtime workload signals to compute interrupt budgets.

Key components:
- Soft-state tenant share ledger: credit accrual when tenant waits or uses small-latency requests; credits decay over time to prevent starvation. Credits are simple numeric tokens attached to continuous batches (no persistent metadata).
- Interrupt arbitration module: when a new high-priority request needs a slot, the module scores candidates by (credit, estimated remaining tokens, kv-residency-impact, request-latency-sensitivity) and selects an interrupt target with minimal expected SLO cost.
- Adaptive KV trimming: KV entries are ranked by last-access, estimated future reuse (LRU++ with length/position bias), and memory-pressure scores. Under pressure the system trims cold/KV-prefetch slots and optionally drops less valuable cached key ranges, reclaiming contiguous GPU memory slabs to reduce compaction overhead.
- Cooldown & graceful degrade: interrupted batches are checkpointed to KV-slab-friendly resumable state where possible, and short-lived preemptions use a fast-resume path. Tenants hit repeated preemptions trigger a backoff that increases their credit accrual rate temporarily.

Success criteria / metrics:
- P95 latency for latency-sensitive tenants does not regress by more than 5% under mixed workloads.
- GPU memory pressure-induced compactions reduced by >= 30% vs baseline during 95th percentile load.
- Overall throughput (tokens/sec) drops by <= 7% in mixed latency-sensitive + throughput-heavy workloads.
- Preemption-induced failed/resubmitted requests < 0.5% of total.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs observability: soft-state ledger is intentionally lightweight to avoid persistent coordination. That trades recallability of historic fairness for simpler failure modes.
- Aggressive KV trimming can improve availability but risks quality regressions for long-context models; we mitigate with an optional model-aware weight that penalizes trimming for KV keys associated with hot context prefixes.
- Checkpoint/resume paths add implementation surface on the runtime hot path; we limit scope to short-duration streaming slices to reduce engineering risk.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement simulation harness and microbenchmarks (single-node and 4-node clusters) — target: 2 weeks.
2) Prototype in batcher-v2 feature-flag behind runtime config; unit tests + fuzzing for ledger correctness — target: 3 weeks.
3) Internal dogfood with synthetic mixed workloads (75/25 latency/throughput) on dedicated cluster with telemetry enabled — 1 week.
4) Canary rollout (5% traffic) with automated guardrails (P95, KV-hit-rate, preempt-count). If stable, 25% then 100% in two-week increments.

Monitoring & alerts:
- New metrics: tenant_credit_balance (gauge), interrupt_score_histogram, kv_trim_rate, resume_path_latency, preempt_count_by_tenant.
- Alerts: kv_trim_rate spike > 2x baseline AND P95 regressions; preempt_count rate > threshold for a tenant with medium/high customer_impact.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for ledger accrual/decay math and interrupt scoring.
- Integration tests simulating sequences with variable sequence length distributions and KV working set churn.
- Loadbench A/B comparing against baseline policies.

Backout criteria: significant P95 regressions (>10%) for latency-sensitive tenants or >10% drop in tokens/sec for SLO-critical clusters.

Notes: This approach favors fairness via soft-state credits and targeted KV trimming rather than rigid tenant reservations. It aims to reduce large memory compactions and provide smoother tail behavior for served applications.
decision: Adopt soft-state tenant shares with adaptive KV trimming and cooldown-driven graceful preemption. Keep ledger ephemeral (in-memory, per-batcher) to avoid distributed coordination. Expose conservative knobs (trim aggressiveness, credit accrual rates) via runtime config for canary tuning.
implementation_steps: Design simulation harness and canonical scenarios
Instrument batcher-v2 with tenant-credit ledger and interrupt-scoring hook
Add KV-trim ranked eviction path and contiguous-slab reclamation
Add resume/fast-resume sequence checkpoint support for short streaming slices
Build dashboards and SLI dashboards for canary monitoring
Run internal dogfood and iterate based on telemetry
Gradual canary rollout with automated rollback conditions
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff: scoped core heuristics and telemetry. Decided to keep ledger in-memory to avoid cross-batcher consensus. Added simulation backlog tasks.
2026-03-04 - Marcus Chen: Engineering review: suggested adding sequence-length-aware weight to KV trimming (to avoid evicting recent long-context tokens). Diego to prototype weighting function.
2026-03-06 - Leah Kim (PM): Confirmed SLO targets for priority tenants; provided representative tenant profiles from customer telemetry.
2026-03-08 - Priya Nair (Infra): Pointed out compaction cost on older GPUs (A100 40GB); recommended contiguous-slab reclamation to avoid repeated cudaMalloc/free churn.

2026-03-10 - Diego Ramos: Prototype complete for ledger + scoring. Early sim shows 28% reduction in compactions and ~4% P95 improvement for latency tenants in mixed workloads. Pushed initial PR for internal review.
2026-03-11 - Review comment (SRE): Add an opt-in config to disable resume checkpointing in clusters with strict determinism requirements. We'll gate resume by runtime flag.
2026-03-12 - Diego Ramos: Updated PR addressing review feedback, added more unit tests for credit decay boundary conditions. Preparing dogfood run next week.
